publicReleaseNotes:
- **Scheduled D1 reads.** The minute cron no longer rereads history when SLA policies, CSAT surveys or webhook and Slack destinations are on. With 30 days of history and all three on, a steady run read about 46,000 to 70,000 D1 rows at 600 conversations and 128,000 to 162,000 at 1,200. It now reads about 80 to 160 rows at either size. Migration 339 adds indexes for open tickets, open SLA alerts, unprepared integration intents, live deliveries and survey discovery, plus the survey cursor table.
- **SLA backstop.** The rolling SLA rebuild reads only open tickets and tickets with an open alert. After a full pass it waits up to an hour before the next one, and starts again straight away when an SLA policy or business calendar changes.
- **Survey discovery.** New CSAT invitations are found from a cursor over resolutions instead of every resolution each minute. A resolution is still rechecked until its invitation would be due.
- **Ticket updates.** Migration 340 stops a reply from moving Inbox count buckets that its old and new times share. A reply read about 1,260 rows and wrote about 470; it now reads about 100 and writes about 150. A ticket edit rebuilds report cohort rows only when a reported field changes.
- **Handle time.** The Handle time panel refreshes every 60 seconds while the tab is visible, and on focus, instead of every 15 seconds in hidden tabs too.
- **Team reports.** Handle time in a team report, and each scheduled team report email, now reads only the handle sessions that overlap the selected dates instead of every session recorded before its end, and no longer rereads the report population once per session. With 600 conversations and one handle session each, a 30-day team report read about 2.1 million D1 rows; it now reads about 77,000, and the figure no longer grows with older history. Migration 339 also indexes handle sessions by end time.
- **Ticket presence.** The presence sweep on an open ticket, every 5 seconds, reuses each stream's authorization for up to a minute. A stream's own messages, replays and deliveries still check the session live, so a revoked or narrowed stream still closes at its next frame and never receives ticket content.
